elements.text: Pilots' failure to ensure the airplane was loaded within weight-and-balance limits
Pilots' attempt to take off with the center of gravity well forward of the forward takeoff limit
Center of gravity position prevented the airplane from rotating at the intended rotation speed
Platinum Jet Management’s conduct of charter flights without proper FAA certification
Platinum Jet Management’s failure to ensure for-hire flights were conducted in accordance with 14 CFR Part 135 requirements
Darby Aviation’s failure to maintain operational control over 14 CFR Part 135 flights conducted by PJM
Operational control failure resulted in an environment conducive to systemic flight crew performance deficiencies
FAA Flight Standards District Office’s failure to provide adequate surveillance and oversight of Darby’s Part 135 operations
FAA’s tacit approval of arrangements between Darby and PJM
Captain had not received training needed to operate 14 CFR Part 135 flights for Darby Aviation
Captain’s reported experience (flight times and previous training) validity was questionable
First officer had not received all required ground training for second-in-command duties
First officer’s Federal Aviation Administration medical certificate had expired for commercial operations
No evidence that fatigue affected the pilots’ performance
Accident airplane was properly certificated and maintained with no preexisting failures
Weather was not a factor in the accident
ARFF response and air traffic controller reaction were prompt and efficient
Doorframe and/or fuselage distortion caused by impact accounted for passengers’ difficulty opening the main cabin door
Platinum Jet Management pilots routinely improperly modified weight and balance forms using invalid empty weights
Airplane was loaded with a forward center of gravity significantly forward of the limit, severely degrading rotation ability
Neither pilot used available weight and balance information appropriately
Pitch trim setting selected by pilots indicated they did not consider the airplane’s center of gravity during preflight
Captain’s decision to initiate rejected takeoff was reasonable
Most line pilots would not have been able to stop the airplane in time to avoid departing the runway
Pilots’ failure to ensure weight and CG were within limits was symptomatic of poor airmanship and crew resource management deficiencies
Darby Aviation failed to maintain operational control over on-demand charter flights conducted by PJM
Lack of rigorous enforcement of operational control allowed PJM pilots to operate in an environment where preflight errors were less likely to be detected
FAA’s inadequate oversight of the charter management agreement permitted management failures and lack of operational control to exist
FAA oversight failure allowed PJM to operate virtually independently as an on-demand air carrier without demonstrating fitness
Darby Aviation’s FSDO principal inspectors should have requested assistance from a more conveniently located FSDO
FAA failed to perform adequate charter operator surveillance and did not recognize PJM operated as a de facto Part 135 carrier
Lack of clear guidance on agreements allowed unauthorized entities to perform charter functions without proper controls
Cabin aide did not perform a seatbelt compliance check, resulting in unrestrained passengers
Intentional positioning of seatbelts made them difficult to locate, reducing compliance
Cabin aide’s training did not adequately prepare her for duties including opening the main cabin door
Installation of EMAS would provide additional safety margin but would not have prevented the accident
